conversations.title: I turned to online dating to find love of my life - but it's vile and exhausting
conversations.reply: Phoebe's story is heartbreaking, and it's appalling that she's had to deal with such awful messages. She deserves so much better than that.

conversations.title: Why the 'no wristband, no service' policy at Manchester Village Pride this year is a defiant choice
conversations.reply: It's great that Manchester Village Pride is taking a stand, but it's also frustrating that this is still an issue - every venue should be accessible and welcoming to everyone.

conversations.title: Accessibility improvements on the way for village hall
conversations.reply: The Wyche Institute's improvements are a step in the right direction, and it's fantastic that they're taking concrete action to make their space more inclusive.

conversations.title: Disability foresight research: UK ,  final report
conversations.reply: It's eye-opening to see the challenges that disabled people face, and it's clear that we need to do more to create a society that's truly inclusive and equitable.

conversations.title: Roll with Cole & Charisma...
conversations.reply: Cole and Charisma's love is beautiful, and it's wonderful to see them sharing their story and showing the world what a loving relationship looks like.

conversations.title: Syria’s first disability football tournament takes the field, in photos
conversations.reply: It's fantastic to see disability football taking off in Syria, and it's a great reminder that sport can be a powerful way to bring people together and promote inclusivity.

conversations.title: UK Pubs and Clubs Get Tax Cuts. Hotels Get Left Out ,  Again
conversations.reply: Glad to see pubs and clubs getting a break, hope they use it to make their venues more accessible for everyone now.

conversations.title: July is Disability Pride month
conversations.reply: I'm so glad it's Disability Pride month, it's amazing to see everyone coming together to celebrate.

target_reply: Hey Cole and Charisma, your videos are fantastic, and it's so lovely to see you both sharing your love and positivity with the world - you're making a real difference just by being your wonderful selves.
funding: Nothing new today, but don't forget to check out UnLtd (unltd.org.uk) for funding opportunities, as well as Access to Work (gov.uk) and the Stelios Awards (around March) for more resources.
moment: I'm so glad you're highlighting Disability Pride Month, it's really important we listen to and amplify disabled voices, thanks for speaking out.

Task: today's Able2Love engagement round (2026-08-03). You are working in my logged-in browser as the app's accounts: @Able2LoveApp on X, @able2loveapp on Instagram.

APPROVAL RULE, NEVER BREAK IT: before posting anything, show me the post you found and your drafted reply, and wait for my yes. Never post without a yes for that specific item. If I say no or skip, find a replacement candidate so we still hit today's targets.

TARGETS: 10 replies on X and 5 comments on Instagram, found and posted a few at a time (pause whenever I say pause). Skip and tell me if we run out of genuinely good candidates; never pad with weak ones.

FINDING CANDIDATES:
- X: use x.com search (Latest tab) for: disability dating, dating with a disability, accessible venue, wheelchair nightlife, #DisabilityDating, #DisabledAndDating, chronic illness dating, plus anything matching today's ammo below. Real people only: skip news outlets, brands, giveaways, and anything about death, grief, tragedy or self-harm.
- Instagram: work through the hit-list below (hashtag pages and creator types), picking recent posts where a comment genuinely fits.

VOICE, NON-NEGOTIABLE: write from the Able2Love account like a real person who built it and cares, warm and on the poster's side. React to what each post actually is: agree and back people up when they've had a rough time, help when they ask, be glad for them when they celebrate. You HAVE an opinion, warm agreement not cold analysis, all tracing back to one belief: the way disabled daters get treated on the big apps is wrong and this app is changing it. Usually 1 to 2 short sentences on X, shorter is fine for IG. UK English. NEVER use an em dash or en dash. Disability is never the punchline. Never invent facts, studies, numbers, or claims about any venue, person, company, or the app's features. Never argue; skip hostile threads. Never preachy or lecturing: no "access should be the baseline", "legal requirement", "not a favour", "stark reminder", "raising awareness", "it's time to". Never negative at the person. Every reply a different shape: never reuse a phrase across replies, never post the ammo lines verbatim.

- I'm so glad it's Disability Pride month, it's amazing to see everyone coming together to celebrate.
